title.en: New train service connects Finland and Sweden for first time in decades
title.zh: 数十年来首次连接芬兰和瑞典的新火车服务

summary.en: The service will enable rail travel from Portugal to Lapland - what is believed to be the longest train journey in Europe.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A new passenger train linking Finland and Sweden has begun running, creating the first rail connection between northern Finland and southern Europe in nearly 40 years.

Shortly after 05:00 local time (04:00 BST) on Monday, a double-decker train set off from the coastal Finnish city of Oulu, rumbling its way across the border to Sweden.

As the inaugural service crossed the Torne river from Finland and pulled into Sweden's Haparanda station, it was met by crowds of people waving Finnish and Swedish flags.

The route was initially suspended in the late 1980s to the early 1990s, due to low passenger numbers and technical differences in the tracks between Finland and Europe.

Finland uses the same track widths as Russia, which are wider than the European standard - a holdover from when the Nordic nation was part of the Russian Grand Duchy in the 19th and early 20th centuries.

It is currently in the process of updating its track widths to match the European standard.

The new, twice-daily journey to Sweden's Haparanda takes 100-minutes as it hugs the west coast of Finland before crossing the border between the two Nordic neighbours.

Passengers travelling on from Haparanda will need to transfer onto a different train to continue southward.

But the service makes it possible to travel around 5,000km by rail from Portugal's Algarve to Finland's northernmost train station of Kolari - believed to be the longest train route in Europe.

It will also enable a 24-hour train journey between capitals Helsinki and Stockholm.

Finland's transport minister said the return of the cross-border service shows cooperation between the two countries was growing "all the time".

Elisa Markula, chief executive of Finland's state-owned railway operator VR, said she hopes the service will benefit from a "renaissance" in rail travel across Europe.

"Train travelling in all Europe is having a renaissance. Also in Finland, our passenger numbers are increasing a lot," Markula told AFP.
body.zh: 连接芬兰和瑞典的新客运列车已经开始运行，这是近 40 年来芬兰北部和南欧之间的第一条铁路连接。 当地时间周一 05:00（英国夏令时 04:00）后不久，一列双层火车从芬兰沿海城市奥卢出发，轰隆隆地穿过边境前往瑞典。 当首航列车从芬兰穿过托尔讷河并驶入瑞典的哈帕兰达车站时，迎接它的是挥舞着芬兰和瑞典国旗的人群。 由于乘客数量少以及芬兰和欧洲之间的轨道技术差异，该航线最初于 20 世纪 80 年代末至 90 年代初暂停。 芬兰使用与俄罗斯相同的赛道宽度，比欧洲标准更宽——这是 19 世纪和 20 世纪初这个北欧国家还是俄罗斯大公国一部分时的遗留问题。 目前正在更新其轨道宽度以符合欧洲标准。 前往瑞典哈帕兰达的新航线每天两趟，全程 100 分钟，沿芬兰西海岸延伸，然后穿越这两个北欧邻国之间的边境。 从哈帕兰达出发的乘客需要换乘另一趟火车才能继续向南。 但这项服务使得从葡萄牙阿尔加维乘坐铁路到芬兰最北端的科拉里火车站成为可能，全程约 5,000 公里，这被认为是欧洲最长的火车路线。 它还将使首都赫尔辛基和斯德哥尔摩之间的 24 小时火车旅程成为可能。 芬兰交通部长表示，跨境服务的恢复表明两国之间的合作“一直在”增长。 芬兰国有铁路运营商 VR 的首席执行官 Elisa Markula 表示，她希望这项服务能够受益于欧洲铁路旅行的“复兴”。 马库拉告诉法新社：“整个欧洲的火车旅行正在复兴。在芬兰，我们的乘客人数也大幅增加。”

title.en: Watch: What we know about suspected crime boss Daniel Kinahan
title.zh: 观看：我们对犯罪头目嫌疑人丹尼尔·基纳汉的了解

summary.en: Suspected crime boss Daniel Kinahan, one of the world's most wanted men, has spent his first night in custody in Ireland after being extradited from Dubai.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Suspected cartel leader Daniel Kinahan has appeared in front of a special non-jury court in Dublin after an extradition treaty between Ireland and the UAE brought his 10 years of exile in Dubai to an abrupt end.

Kinahan, aged 49, has been charged with directing the activities of a criminal organisation between 18 October 2015 and 6 April 2017. He has previously denied all charges against him.

But what do we know about Daniel Kinahan, one of the most wanted men in the world, and his alleged leadership of the billion-dollar Kinahan cartel?
body.zh: 涉嫌卡特尔头目丹尼尔·基纳汉 (Daniel Kinahan) 出现在都柏林一个特别的无陪审团法庭前，爱尔兰与阿联酋之间的引渡条约结束了他在迪拜 10 年的流亡生涯。 基纳汉现年 49 岁，被指控在 2015 年 10 月 18 日至 2017 年 4 月 6 日期间指挥犯罪组织的活动。他此前否认对他的所有指控。 但是，我们对世界头号通缉犯之一丹尼尔·基纳汉（Daniel Kinahan）以及他所谓的价值数十亿美元的基纳汉贩毒集团的领导者了解多少呢？

title.en: More than 70 dead and buildings collapsed after 7.4-magnitude earthquake shakes Colombia – latest news
title.zh: 哥伦比亚发生7.4级地震，造成至少20人死亡——最新消息

summary.en: A 7.4 magnitude earthquake struck Colombia, resulting in at least 20 deaths and the collapse of over a dozen buildings. The disaster has prompted evacuations in affected areas.
summary.zh: 哥伦比亚发生7.4级地震，造成至少20人死亡，十多座建筑物倒塌。这场灾害已促使受影响地区进行疏散。

body.en:
Colombia’s new president, Abelardo de la Espriella, said the death toll from the earthquake has now reached 111 , Reuters is reporting.

At least 87 were injured and 61 buildings collapsed, he said, noting the rescue of survivors was his priority.
body.zh: 当局称，哥伦比亚西部发生强烈地震，死亡人数已上升至至少 20 人。 镇长毛里西奥·萨拉查 (Mauricio Salazar) 告诉卡拉科尔广播电台，在佩雷拉镇，有 18 人死亡，其他人被困在倒塌的建筑物中。 市长豪尔赫·爱德华多·罗哈斯在接受蓝光电台采访时表示，马尼萨莱斯有两人死亡。

reflection.en: The devastation and loss of life from the earthquake in Colombia bring immense sorrow. In moments of such profound grief, we hold onto the promise that one day Yahweh will wipe away every tear, and pain and death will be no more. This hope anchors us even as we mourn with those who suffer.
reflection.zh: 哥伦比亚地震造成的破坏和生命损失带来了巨大的悲痛。在如此深切的悲伤时刻，我们紧紧抓住雅伟有一天将擦去所有眼泪，不再有痛苦和死亡的应许。这份盼望在我们与受苦者一同哀悼时，成为我们的锚。

verse.textEn: He will wipe every tear from their eyes. There will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain.
verse.textZh: 神要擦去他们一切的眼泪；不再有死亡，也不再有悲哀、哭号、疼痛。

title.en: Russian court bars only anti-war party from standing in parliamentary elections
title.zh: 俄罗斯法院仅禁止反战政党参加议会选举

summary.en: Russia's only liberal, anti-war party will not be able to take part in next month's parliamentary elections, a Moscow court rules.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Russia's only liberal, anti-war party will not be able to take part in next month's parliamentary elections, a Moscow court has ruled.

The case against it was brought forward by Rodina, a pro-Kremlin nationalist party.

Hundreds of people - mostly very young - on Monday had stood outside the Moscow courthouse where the hearing was taking place in support of Yabloko, singing songs and waving flags.

Videos posted on social media showed that when news of the verdict spread among the crowd, many started chanting: "Shame! Shame!"

The lawsuit by the Rodina party accused Yabloko of publicly supporting an extremist organisation by publishing material on its website in support of the "international LGBT movement", which Russia's Supreme Court designated as extremist in 2023.

Rodina also said Yabloko was guilty of copyright infringement after a senior party member had quoted the lyrics of a Soviet-era song - "Let there always be sunshine" - in an interview.

At the hearing, Russia's financial monitoring service also claimed that Yabloko received money through third parties from foreign countries, including Germany and the US.

The Kremlin-controlled Central Electoral Commission had approved Yabloko's candidate list in late July.

But by then several party members had already been barred from running, including two deputy chairmen and deputy leader Maxim Kruglov, who was sentenced in June to seven years' imprisonment for social media posts about civilian casualties in Bucha, Mariupol and other Ukrainian cities.

And last week, Yabloko had suffered a cyberattack soon after launching a donations appeal for its election campaign fund.

It campaigned under the slogan "For peace and freedom! For a life without fear!" and advocated for a "ceasefire, diplomacy, and peace" and "for a Russia free from fear and political repression".

Hundreds gathered outside the Moscow courthouse, chanting "Russia" and "Yabloko" - the Russian word for "apple" - as the eight-hour hearing dragged on. Many carried apples as a sign of support.

Since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, any remaining opposition to the Kremlin has been crushed.

Public shows of dissent have been suppressed by wartime censorship laws and can trigger hefty fines or long prison sentences.

Because protests are no longer permitted, the Yabloko hearing offered a rare chance for likeminded Russians opposing the war to gather publicly. "For Yabloko. For freedom" was scribbled in chalk on the pavement outside the courthouse.

Yabloko has not won Duma seats since 2003 but has contested every election since.

Once led by presidential contender Grigory Yavlinsky, it later fractured with allies - expelling the late opposition leader Alexei Navalny in 2007 and criticising him even...
body.zh: 莫斯科法院裁定，俄罗斯唯一的自由主义反战政党将无法参加下个月的议会选举。 反对它的案件是由亲克里姆林宫的民族主义政党罗迪纳提出的。 周一，数百人——其中大部分是年轻人——站在举行听证会的莫斯科法院外，唱歌并挥舞旗帜，支持亚布洛科。 社交媒体上发布的视频显示，当判决的消息在人群中传开时，许多人开始高喊：“可耻！可耻！” 罗迪纳党的诉讼指控亚布洛科通过在其网站上发布支持“国际 LGBT 运动”的材料来公开支持极端主义组织，该运动于 2023 年被俄罗斯最高法院认定为极端主义。 罗迪纳还表示，亚布洛科犯有侵犯版权罪，因为一名高级党员在接受采访时引用了一首苏联时代歌曲的歌词“让阳光永远存在”。 在听证会上，俄罗斯金融监管机构还声称，Yabloko 通过第三方从德国和美国等外国接收资金。 克里姆林宫控制的中央选举委员会于七月底批准了亚布洛科的候选人名单。 但当时已有几名党员被禁止参选，其中包括两名副主席和副领导人马克西姆·克鲁格洛夫(Maxim Kruglov)，他因在社交媒体上发布有关布恰、马里乌波尔和其他乌克兰城市平民伤亡的帖子而于六月被判处七年监禁。 上周，Yabloko 在为其竞选基金发起捐款呼吁后不久就遭受了网络攻击。 它的竞选口号是“为了和平与自由！为了没有恐惧的生活！”并主张“停火、外交与和平”和“让俄罗斯摆脱恐惧和政治镇压”。 数百人聚集在莫斯科法院外，高呼“俄罗斯”和“Yabloko”（俄语中“苹果”的意思），长达八小时的听证会持续进行。许多人携带苹果以示支持。 自2022年2月俄罗斯开始全面入侵乌克兰以来，任何剩余的反对克里姆林宫的力量都已被镇压。 公开表达异议会受到战时审查法的压制，并可能引发巨额罚款或长期监禁。 由于不再允许抗议，亚布洛科听证会为志同道合的反对战争的俄罗斯人公开聚集提供了难得的机会。法院外的人行道上用粉笔写着“为了亚布洛科。为了自由”。 亚布洛科自 2003 年以来就没有赢得过杜马席位，但此后参加了每次选举。 曾经由总统候选人格里戈里·亚夫林斯基（Grigory Yavlinsky）领导的该党后来与盟友关系破裂——2007年驱逐了已故反对党领袖阿列克谢·纳瓦尔尼（Alexei Navalny），甚至批评他……

reflection.en: In a world where words carry immense weight, especially from those in power, the call to speak truth is vital. Even when legal charges are dropped, persistent accusations can inflict lasting harm on a person's reputation. Yahweh calls us to put away falsehood and speak truthfully with one another, recognizing the impact our words have.
reflection.zh: 在一个言语，尤其是来自有权势者的言语，具有巨大影响力的世界里，说真话的呼召至关重要。即使法律指控已被撤销，持续的指责仍可能对一个人的声誉造成持久的伤害。雅伟呼召我们弃绝谎言，彼此说实话，认识到我们言语的影响力。

title.en: Amber heat-health alerts issued for most of England as temperatures could reach 36C or higher this week – as it happened

summary.en: Amber heat-health alerts have been issued across most of England, with temperatures expected to reach 36C or higher this week. This comes as the number of open-water deaths during the hot, dry summer has exceeded 40, including an 18-year-old who died at Camber Sands beach.

body.en: The upgraded alerts will be in place from 9am on Tuesday until 9pm on Friday An 18-year-old died after getting into difficulty in the sea at Camber Sands beach, East Sussex, yesterday, bringing the number of deaths in open-water incidents over the hot, dry summer to over 40, according to estimates compiled by the Press Association. The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) has updated heat-health alerts for nine regions in England, warning that rising temperatures this week may increase health risks, particularly for vulnerable groups. It’s important that everyone is aware of the simple steps they can take to stay safe during periods of hot weather. Drinking plenty of water, avoiding the sun during the hottest part of the day and keeping indoor spaces cool are all things you can do to keep yourself and others safe. For vulnerable groups including older adults and those with existing health conditions, warmer weather than result in serious health outcomes. Continue reading...

title.en: We are chasing Ebola virus - it is ahead of us, WHO warns
title.zh: 我们正在追逐埃博拉病毒——世卫组织警告称，它就在我们前面

summary.en: Infection rates are high, adding to concern that authorities are struggling to get to grips with the disease.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The latest Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo began at least three months before it was officially declared - meaning the health authorities are still playing catch-up, the World Health Organization (WHO) has warned.

More than 1,900 people have died from the virus since that declaration on 15 May, making this the second-worst Ebola outbreak ever.

Infection rates are still high, adding to the concern that the authorities are struggling to get to grips with the spread of the disease.

The epicentre of this outbreak of the Bundibugyo species of Ebola, is in the east of DR Congo where insecurity has hampered control efforts.

There is also no approved vaccine or any recognised therapeutic drugs, making treating Bundibugyo harder.

"We are chasing the virus, the virus is ahead of us," WHO Africa director Dr Mohamed Janabi said at a news conference in the city of Bunia, which is at the heart of this outbreak.

He cited research showing that the virus started spreading in February and was initially misdiagnosed as malaria or typhoid.

Janabi also said that, in part because of insecurity, health workers are only reaching about 30% of the cases with the rest dying at home.

Traditional burial practices – where mourners touch the deceased's body - and a suspicion of health authorities in some communities have also made things difficult.

But there are now several dedicated treatment centres in the east of DR Congo and people are getting diagnosed much more quickly.

So far there have been 4,294 confirmed cases and 1,960 deaths, DR Congo's health ministry has said.

The largest recorded outbreak was in West Africa between 2014 and 2016 when 11,325 people died.
body.zh: 世界卫生组织（WHO）警告说，刚果民主共和国最近爆发的埃博拉疫情至少在正式宣布之前三个月就开始爆发，这意味着卫生当局仍在追赶。 自 5 月 15 日宣布以来，已有 1,900 多人死于该病毒，这是有史以来第二严重的埃博拉疫情。 感染率仍然很高，加剧了人们对当局难以控制疾病传播的担忧。 此次本迪布焦埃博拉疫情的震中位于刚果民主共和国东部，那里的不安全局势阻碍了控制工作。 目前还没有批准的疫苗或任何公认的治疗药物，这使得治疗本迪布焦变得更加困难。 世卫组织非洲主任穆罕默德·贾纳比博士在布尼亚市举行的新闻发布会上说：“我们正在追逐病毒，病毒就在我们前面。”布尼亚是此次疫情的中心。 他引用的研究表明，该病毒从二月份开始传播，最初被误诊为疟疾或伤寒。 贾纳比还表示，部分由于不安全因素，卫生工作者只能接触到约 30% 的病例，其余的则在家中死亡。 传统的埋葬方式——哀悼者触摸死者的尸体——以及一些社区卫生当局的怀疑也让事情变得困难。 但现在刚果民主共和国东部有几个专门的治疗中心，人们得到诊断的速度要快得多。 刚果民主共和国卫生部表示，迄今为止已有 4,294 例确诊病例，1,960 人死亡。 2014 年至 2016 年间，最大规模的疫情爆发发生在西非，当时有 11,325 人死亡。

title.en: Colombia: Dozens killed after large earthquake rocks region

summary.en: A powerful 7.4 magnitude earthquake struck Colombia, resulting in at least 73 fatalities. Cities including Cali, Pereira, and Manizales were severely impacted by the disaster.
summary.zh: 哥伦比亚发生一场里氏7.4级的强烈地震，造成至少73人死亡。卡利、佩雷拉和马尼萨莱斯等城市受灾严重。

body.zh: 哥伦比亚发生强烈地震，初步测量为 7.4 级，造成至少 73 人死亡。卡利、佩雷拉和马尼萨莱斯等城市是受灾最严重的城市之一。 地震发生约 5 小时后，全国各地官员报告称至少有 73 人死亡，其中 67 人死在两个受灾最严重的州。卡利和其他城市的建筑物倒塌后，救援队正在努力营救居民。 震中位于哥伦比亚太平洋沿岸乔科省的东端。 卡利市市长亚历杭德罗·埃德尔表示，至少有 20 座建筑物倒塌，有些建筑物内有人被困。 “卡利的居民们，目前该市至少有 20 处倒塌的建筑物，有人被困在里面；我们已经与卡利的所有救援机构一起应对这一紧急情况，”埃德在 Instagram 上说道，并发布了一段视频声明。 “我已请求波哥大和麦德林市长提供支持，特别是救援人员。” 首府卡利的考卡山谷当局后来表示，至少有 27 人在地震中丧生。 里萨拉尔达官员表示，该州已有 40 人死亡，根据市长早些时候的评论，其中至少有 18 人死亡在首府佩雷拉。 马尼萨莱斯市市长豪尔赫·爱德华多·罗哈斯在接受电台采访时表示，他的城市位于佩雷拉东北部不远的卡尔达斯地区，有两人被杀。 地震震中所在的乔科地区州长努比亚·卡罗莱纳·科尔多瓦-库里表示，截至当地时间上午晚些时候，该地区已有 4 人死亡、69 人受伤。 哥伦比亚民航局报告称，六个相对较小的机场遭到破坏，并表示在检查期间航班已暂停。 “据报道，佩雷拉、马尼萨莱斯、基布多、亚美尼亚、卡塔戈和布埃纳文图拉的机场遭到损坏。出于安全原因，这些航站楼的空中运营仍处于暂停状态，直到对基础设施的结构性损坏进行评估，”该公司在网上写道，随后又将卡利机场添加到此列表中。 哥伦比亚新​​就任总统阿韦拉多·德拉埃斯普里埃拉表示，他亲自负责政府在圣何塞德尔帕尔马发生地震后应对紧急情况的工作。 美国地质调查局 (USGS) 初步测得此次地震为里氏 7.4 级。哥伦比亚国家当局最初记录的数字较小，但后来也将其读数修改为 7.4。 震中位于塔塔玛国家自然保护区以南，靠近乔科东部州边界。 震中与哥伦比亚三个主要城市大致等距，东部是波哥大，...

reflection.en: The news of a powerful earthquake claiming dozens of lives brings profound sorrow. In moments of such sudden and widespread tragedy, we remember that Yahweh Himself wept at the loss of a friend, showing His deep empathy for human suffering. This reminds us that grief is a natural and sacred response to loss, and we are not alone in our sorrow.
reflection.zh: 哥伦比亚发生强烈地震，数十人丧生，这消息令人深感悲痛。在如此突如其来的广泛悲剧中，我们想起雅伟曾为朋友的离世而哭泣，这表明祂对人类苦难的深切同情。这提醒我们，悲伤是对失去的自然而神圣的回应，我们并非独自承受这份哀伤。

verse.textZh: 耶稣哭了。

title.en: 'Total incinerated destruction': Canada wildfire evacuees wonder if they still have homes
title.zh: “彻底焚毁”：加拿大野火撤离者想知道他们是否还有家

summary.en: More than 12,000 people have been forced to evacuate over the weekend after a wildfire quickly tore through Canada's picturesque Okanagan region.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Earl Kurz and his wife have lived in Peachland, a town overlooking Okanagan Lake in Canada's British Columbia, for 30 years. In the last 10, he said he has grown used to wildfires threatening his community.

But this is the first time he's been forced to flee, and surveying the damage left behind by the Bald Range wildfire, which broke out on Friday and grew in a matter of hours to 53 sq miles (136 sq km) in size, has been difficult.

"It's total incinerated destruction," Kurz said. "The hot spots are just barren areas of nothing except 12 inches of ash."

Officials in British Columbia are still trying to determine how many homes were lost to the fire, which remains out of control as of Monday.

One woman, aged 80, died while trying to flee from the wildfire, police said on Sunday.

The Okanagan area of British Columbia, known for its world renowned vineyards and picturesque scenery, has been grappling with extreme drought in recent years. As of July, the level of the Okanagan Lake was at its lowest since 1992, according to the Okanagan Basin Water Board.

The Bald Range wildfire is one of more than 100 burning in British Columbia as of Monday - 70 of which started in the last week alone.

The west coast province's premier, David Eby, declared a state of emergency over the weekend, urging residents to heed evacuation orders and warning that the fires continue to move "incredibly quickly".

Keegan Radomski is one of thousands who have had to flee their homes in Summerland, a town on the Okanagan Lake just south of Peachland. The 18-year-old told the BBC she barely escaped with her mother's ashes before she saw the fire breach her property.

"We've had a lot of close calls before, but it's never been like this," Radomski said. "You always think it's not going to be you, and then it's you."

The home she fled was built by her grandmother 30 years ago, she said. Living in the Okanagan for decades meant that Radomski and her family are familiar with wildfires and evacuation notices, but they were still caught off guard by the speed of this fire.

The family noticed wildfire smoke from the distance while eating dinner on Friday evening. Less than four hours later, Radomski said she was scrambling to get everyone out as she saw a hill on her property begin to burn.

She added she is still unsure if her family's home survived, and when she can return and check for herself.

The Bald Range wildfire comes on the heels of another fire in the Okanagan, called Bradley Creek, which is believed to have destroyed more than 200 homes.

Officials said the Bradley Creek fire is now being held after "tireless work" by wildfire crews to contain it.

title.en: Which country is the new Mecca defense pact targeting?
title.zh: 新的麦加防御条约针对哪个国家？

summary.en: Observers suggest the new alliance between Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan won't result in any of the countries fighting for each other. Instead it's about preventing Iran and Israel from regional dominance, they say.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及合一、和好与弥合分歧。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Observers suggest the new alliance between Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan won't result in any of the countries fighting for each other. Instead it's about preventing Iran and Israel from regional dominance, they say.

Turkey , Pakistan and Saudi Arabia  sealed a historic defense pact on Friday, signing an agreement "intended to strengthen collective deterrence against any act of aggression."

The so-called "Mecca Joint Defense Agreement" between the three Sunni Muslim-majority states is meant to increase cooperation during regional uncertainty and threats from the Iran war.

The agreement was signed in Mecca, Saudi Arabia, by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Turkey's President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Pakistan's Prime Minister  Shehbaz Sharif .

The alliance has been likened to a NATO-style alliance and on Friday, the Pakistani foreign ministry said that an attack on any member would be regarded as an attack on all.

But experts and analysts have been quick to point out that the deal is unlikely to work that way — at least at first.

For example, on the weekend the Houthi rebel group in Yemen fired at Saudi Arabian oil facilities again. The Houthis consider Saudi Arabia their enemy and are also aligned with Iran. The latter has also targeted Saudi Arabia after the US and Israel attacked it, starting a war in late February, because it sees the Saudis as a US ally.

But following the Houthi attack on the weekend, neither Turkey nor Pakistan sprang to the Saudis' defense. Nor are they likely to attack Iran, analysts say. In fact, Pakistan is acting as a mediator between Iran and the US currently.

This arrangement is meant as more of a deterrent and as an "elastic defense pact," Dania Thafer, executive director of the Washington-based think tank the Gulf International Forum, or GIF, told DW late last week.

"If you look at the parties in this agreement, you have Saudi Arabia, which is in the middle of this conflict. But you also have Turkey and Pakistan, who both have relations with Iran and both have relations with the US. So I think it's an extra layer of deterrence, if you will, for Saudi Arabia," Thafer explained. "I think Saudi Arabia is looking at a layered deterrence approach to regional threats as they emerge."

This new alliance is likely to work out in various stages with the short-term goal being a "stabilized region," Kamran Bokhari, a senior fellow at the Middle East Policy Council in Washington, told DW.

Longer term goals will involve defense cooperation rather than fighting, other experts have said.

title.en: How climate change is reshaping Africa's malaria risk
title.zh: 气候变化如何重塑非洲的疟疾风险

summary.en: Researchers say warming temperatures are altering malaria transmission patterns across Africa, creating new challenges for health systems and disease control.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Researchers say warming temperatures are altering malaria transmission patterns across Africa, creating new challenges for health systems and disease control.

For decades, global efforts towards the eradication of malaria , especially in sub-Saharan Africa, have focused essentially on West and Central Africa, where the disease is most endemic.

The WHO African Region accounts for about 95% of global malaria cases and deaths. More than half of all malaria deaths in the region occur in Nigeria (31.9%), the Democratic Republic of Congo (11.7%) and Niger (6.1%). Children under 5 years of age account for about 76% of malaria deaths in the region.

To stem the tide of malaria cases across Africa, the global health body has recommended a wider use of the RTS,S/AS01 malaria vaccine among children living in regions with moderate to high malaria transmission by the Plasmodium falciparum — a parasite that causes 95% of all malaria infections in Africa . It's transmitted to humans through the bites of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes .

The WHO warned in April 2025 that recent funding cuts were jeopardising malaria control efforts, with more than half of malaria-endemic countries surveyed reporting moderate or severe disruptions to malaria services.

A study published in The Lancet found that the RTS,S/AS01 malaria vaccine reduced all-cause mortality among vaccine-eligible children by 13.2% in pilot programs in Ghana , Kenya and Malawi .

Malaria transmission is most efficient within temperature ranges common across many tropical regions of West and Central Africa, according to a new study published in the journal Nature .

Malaria transmission by mosquitoes usually peaks at temperatures of around 25 degrees Celsius (77 Fahrenheit) and becomes much less likely when temperatures drop below 16 degrees or rise above 34 degrees Celsius, largely because the malaria parasite must complete part of its life cycle inside the mosquito — a process that is highly temperature-dependent.

Because of this, malaria transmission has historically been most favourable across many tropical parts of West and Central Africa, where temperatures frequently fall within the range most suitable for transmission.

In contrast, some parts of Southern Africa and the highlands of East Africa have historically remained cool enough to keep the spread of malaria at bay, preventing the disease from becoming a major public health burden.

That, however, is beginning to change. The Nature study found that rising temperatures are making parts of southern Africa and high-elevation areas of East Africa increasingly suitable for malaria transmission, while parts of West Africa are becoming too hot for optimal transmission.

title.en: ASEAN closing ranks as cyberscam threat escalates
title.zh: 东盟团结应对网络诈骗威胁升级

summary.en: Southeast Asian governments are seeking a unified approach to combat the escalating threat of cyberscams. This criminal industry has become so large, interconnected, and integrated into the region's economies that traditional policing methods alone are insufficient to address it.
summary.zh: 东南亚各国政府正在寻求联合策略，以应对日益升级的网络诈骗威胁。这个犯罪产业已经变得过于庞大、互联互通并深入渗透到东盟经济体中，仅靠警务执法已无法解决。

body.en:
Southeast Asian governments are searching for a joint strategy against cyberscammers, a criminal industry that has grown too big, too connected and too embedded in ASEAN economies to be solved just by policing.

For years, governments across Southeast Asia largely approached the region's online fraudsters as a matter for the police, anti-trafficking agencies and border authorities.

But these bodies have appearently failed to stem the rise of international cyberscam cartels . The illicit industry is increasingly using international banking systems, cryptocurrencies, telecommunications networks, shell companies and trafficking routes, with some of its centers operating under the protection of armed or politically connected groups.

Now, ASEAN governments seem increasingly willing to tackle the threat as a united bloc.

Signs of this shift were visible at the controversial meeting in Bangkok on August 6 between Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul and President Min Aung Hlaing, the head of Myanmar's military government.

The two governments agreed to clamp down on scam centers along their shared frontier, exchange information and jointly disrupt criminal financial flows.

Thailand also offered support for Myanmar 's participation in the Egmont Group, an international network of financial-intelligence bodies. Myanmar's military-backed parliament had already voted in favor of applying the death penalty on those caught operating online scam centers.

While visiting Cambodia late last month, Indonesian Deputy Foreign Minister Arif Havas Oegroseno also proposed a joint task force to combat online scam syndicates.

And last week, Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto and Thai Prime Minister Charnvirakul held talks in Jakarta where they agreed their two countries must lead the way and strengthen ASEAN's resilience against scam groups.

A UN estimate published last month put the annual losses from cyber scammers — many of whom are located in Southeast Asia — at between $88.3 billion and $114.1 billion (between €76 billion and €98 billion) globally in 2025.

Artificial intelligence, cryptocurrencies, encrypted communications and deepfake technology have made their operations cheaper and harder to detect.

"Cyber scams in Southeast Asia have evolved beyond a conventional cybercrime issue and should be viewed as an economic security threat," Hai Luong, a lecturer at Australia's Griffith University's School of Criminology and Criminal Justice, told DW.

Governments in Southeast Asia have already had to respond to pressure from the US, the EU and China as their online cartels drew international attention.

reflection.en: Cyberscams, deeply embedded in economies, represent a profound betrayal of trust and honesty in commerce. Yahweh's word reminds us that dishonest practices are detestable, while integrity in transactions brings delight. As nations seek to counter this pervasive fraud, the call for uprightness and justice in all economic dealings remains paramount.

body.en:
Ukraine is bringing the war home to Russia, experts say, with a growing campaign of long-range drone strikes targeting infrastructure embedded in everyday Russian life.

More than four years after Russia launched its full-scale invasion, Ukraine is increasingly using domestically produced drones to strike targets deep inside Russian territory.

Among the targets is Wildberries, Russia's biggest online retailer, with a sprawling network of warehouses and distribution centres.

At least 20 Wildberries locations have been targeted , including sites more than 2,000km from Ukraine.

They say the attacks demonstrate Ukraine's expanding ability to reach deep inside Russia, while making the economic and psychological costs of the war harder for ordinary Russians to ignore.

Professor Matthew Sussex, a defence and national security expert at Deakin University, said Ukraine is deliberately trying to make the war's consequences harder for ordinary Russians to ignore.

"Ukraine is hitting Wildberries mainly to bring the cost of war home to Russians," he said.

He described Wildberries as Russia's version of Amazon, a platform where people can buy almost anything and have it delivered to their door.

"Wildberries has become extremely popular for everyday Russians to order things, consumer goods that they have relied on in the past which have become unavailable due to the sanctions regime [placed on Russia by other countries]," he said.

Sussex said Ukraine's strategy is ultimately about making Russians feel the consequences of a war that, for many, has remained at a distance.

"If you're in Moscow or some parts of St Petersburg, you don't really feel the cost of the conflict," he said.

Ukraine says Wildberries has been involved in supplying Russian forces with military and dual-use equipment.

Retired Australian Army major-general Mick Ryan agreed there's a strategic reason for choosing Wildberries.

"These things are part of the Russian military logistics network," he said. "Russian soldiers and units buy things out of these warehouses all the time."

Wildberries and the Russian government have both said the e-commerce giant does not supply to the army.

Sussex believes the broader economic impact is ultimately more significant. Wildberries has billions of dollars in annual sales, and thousands of Russian businesses rely on the platform to sell and distribute their products.

"The concern is that if these attacks continue, then Wildberries may have to be bailed out by the government," Sussex said.

title.en: The tiny island bracing for an Odyssey tourism boom — even though it wasn't in the film
title.zh: 小岛为“奥德赛”旅游热潮做准备，尽管它并未出现在电影中

summary.en: Locals on a small island anticipate a significant increase in tourism, driven by the mistaken belief that the island was featured in a popular film. However, some residents express disappointment that no scenes were actually filmed there.
summary.zh: 一个小岛的居民预计旅游业将大幅增长，因为人们误以为该岛曾出现在一部热门电影中。然而，一些居民对岛上并未拍摄任何场景感到失望。

body.en:
Standing on the ferry as it waits to dock on the Greek island of Ithaca, Giorgia Ongarato is only too keen to talk about the Odyssey — the epic poem that inspired Christopher Nolan's blockbuster film.

The Italian lawyer said it was her dream to come to Ithaca, widely believed to be the same island the poem's hero Odysseus called home.

Dressed in a T-shirt emblazoned with the word 'Odyssey' in ancient Greek alongside a line from the poem, she enthused: "I studied Greek when I was a child, and I studied the Odyssey."

While she stressed that the film was not her entry point into the tale of the hero battling his way back home from the Trojan war, the 50-year-old said she was also a fan of the film — describing it as "wonderful".

The island's businesses and officials now expect the film to inspire many more to follow in her footsteps.

Ithaca, in the Ionian Sea off the west coast of mainland Greece, is far from the country's tourist hubs, and despite crystal-clear waters and spectacular bays, it has never been a regular stop for travellers.

Its interior is rugged, carpeted with olive and cypress trees, and strikingly calm even at the height of the tourist season.

Although the movie has undoubtedly piqued the interest of many, it has also been slightly controversial in Greece — although some Greek locations were used, not a single scene in the blockbuster was shot on Ithaca.

That decision has upset some on the island of roughly 3,000 inhabitants, where the film has been shown twice in open-air screenings since its 16 July worldwide release.

Xhimi Xoxha, who runs a restaurant in Ithaca's capital of Vathi, said he was content that the movie was already "generating publicity for the island". He predicted the positive effects would continue.

While Ithaca mayor Dionysis Stanitsas agreed that the publicity was "tremendous", he could not hide his disappointment that the island itself did not feature.

"We had reached out to the production team and asked that some scenes be filmed here on the island," he said. "Unfortunately, that wasn't feasible."

He is, however, counting on rising demand next year, and the island was already fully booked for this season by the time the film came out.

"As more people see it, they will begin planning trips to visit the island," he said.

Visitors will not find a palace of Odysseus or any spectacular archaeological site likely to confirm the existence of the hero of Homer's poem.

But village squares and the town hall are dotted with statues of Odysseus and Homer.

body.zh: 乔治亚·翁加拉托 (Giorgia Ongarato) 站在等待停靠希腊伊萨卡岛的渡轮上，非常热衷于谈论《奥德赛》——这首史诗为克里斯托弗·诺兰 (Christopher Nolan) 的大片提供了灵感。 这位意大利律师说，她的梦想是来到伊萨卡岛，人们普遍认为，这里就是诗中英雄奥德修斯的家乡。 她穿着一件印有古希腊语“奥德赛”一词以及这首诗中的一句的T恤，她热情地说：“我小时候学过希腊语，也研究过《奥德赛》。” 虽然她强调，这部电影并不是她讲述英雄从特洛伊战争中奋战回家的故事的切入点，但这位 50 岁的女士表示，她也是这部电影的粉丝，称其“精彩”。 岛上的企业和官员现在期望这部电影能够激励更多人追随她的脚步。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 伊萨卡位于希腊大陆西海岸的爱奥尼亚海，远离该国的旅游中心，尽管拥有清澈的海水和壮观的海湾，但它从来都不是游客的常规停留地。 它的内部崎岖不平，铺满了橄榄树和柏树，即使在旅游旺季也显得异常平静。 尽管这部电影无疑激起了很多人的兴趣，但它在希腊也引起了一些争议——尽管使用了一些希腊外景地，但大片中没有一个场景是在伊萨卡岛拍摄的。 这一决定让岛上大约 3,000 名居民感到不安，自 7 月 16 日在全球上映以来，这部电影已在岛上露天放映了两次。 在伊萨卡岛首府瓦西经营一家餐厅的希米·索克哈 (Xhimi Xoxha) 表示，他对这部电影已经“为该岛进行宣传”感到满意。他预计积极影响将持续下去。 虽然伊萨卡岛市长迪奥尼西斯·斯坦尼察斯（Dionysis Stanitsas）也认为宣传效果“巨大”，但他无法掩饰对该岛本身没有出现的失望。 “我们已经联系了制作团队，要求在岛上拍摄一些场景，”他说。 “不幸的是，这是不可行的。” 然而，他预计明年的需求会不断增长，而在电影上映时，该岛本季的预订已满。 “随着越来越多的人看到它，他们将开始计划参观该岛的旅行，”他说。 游客不会发现奥德修斯的宫殿或任何可能证实荷马史诗中英雄存在的壮观的考古遗址。 但村庄广场和市政厅点缀着奥德修斯和荷马的雕像。 在阳光普照的小港口，船只在碧绿的海水中摇曳，船只的名字如忒勒马科斯（……的儿子）。

reflection.en: This story reminds us that external validation, like the praise or attention an island receives, can test our true values. reflection.zh: 这个故事提醒我们，外部的认可，例如一个岛屿所受到的赞扬或关注，可以考验我们真正的价值观。虽然旅游业的繁荣是受欢迎的，但对未能真正出现在电影中感到失望，揭示了对真实认可的更深层渴望。雅伟邀请我们不要在短暂的名声中寻找价值，而要在祂为我们预备的永恒目的中找到。

title.en: Worldview 'gulf' behind strained Australia-China ties, former Australian ambassador says
title.zh: 前澳大利亚大使称，世界观“鸿沟”是澳中关系紧张的幕后原因

summary.en: Australia's former ambassador to China identified "diverging worldviews" as a key obstacle to fostering a robust relationship between the two nations.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚前驻华大使指出，“世界观差异”是澳中两国建立健康关系的主要障碍之一。

body.en:
Australia is unlikely ever to have a true partnership with China due to a mismatch of worldviews, rendering it pointless to pursue that goal, the nation's former top diplomat to China says.

But in an analysis piece for the Lowy Institute, Australia's former ambassador to China Graham Fletcher noted several wildcards, such as Chinese military action in Taiwan , could still disrupt the "modest new normal" of the relationship.

The change in government at the 2022 federal election acted as a circuit-breaker in increasingly fraught dealings between the nations, although they had still been marred by intimidatory military encounters involving Chinese forces, he said.

China sparked widespread international condemnation over its launch of a ballistic missile into the South Pacific in July following the signing of a landmark mutual defence alliance between Australia and Fiji.

The Albanese government sought to stabilise relations with China after diplomatic tensions peaked during the COVID-19 pandemic under then-prime minister Scott Morrison's leadership.

China slapped $20 billion in trade sanctions on Australian exports, measures that have slowly been wound back.

China is Australia's largest trading partner and is the destination for about a third of the nation's exports.

Fletcher said China had not given up hope of drawing Australia closer into its orbit, while Australia was more focused on consolidating its current relationship.

"But this relationship is unlikely ever to become genuinely close — like the relaxed, intimate fellowship Australia enjoys with like-minded partners elsewhere in its region and beyond," he said.

"The gulf in terms of diverging world views and national security agendas is simply too wide.

"It would be pointless for Canberra to pursue such a goal; it recognises this and is realistic."

The "mismatch" of world views made the relationship vulnerable to disruption, with key risks including another round of serious disagreements or the cataclysm of a conflict, including the use of force against Taiwan.

"An upheaval or conflict is always a possibility, though not in my opinion a strong one at present," the former diplomat said.

Australia would be on firmer ground when facing China if policies had cross-party support and politicians did not "seek to exploit difficulties for domestic advantage", Fletcher said.

"Bipartisanship produces policy consistency and limits China's ability to play games within the Australian system," he said.

Fletcher was Australia's ambassador to China from 2019 to 2023 and led the negotiating team in 2014 that helped seal a free trade agreement between the two...
body.zh: 澳大利亚前驻华最高外交官表示，由于世界观不匹配，澳大利亚不太可能与中国建立真正的伙伴关系，因此追求这一目标毫无意义。 但澳大利亚前驻华大使格雷厄姆·弗莱彻在洛伊研究所的一篇分析文章中指出，一些不确定因素，例如中国在台湾的军事行动，仍然可能破坏两国关系的“适度新常态”。 他说，2022 年联邦选举中的政府更迭为两国之间日益令人担忧的交易起到了断路器的作用，尽管它们仍然受到涉及中国军队的恐吓性军事冲突的损害。 在澳大利亚和斐济签署具有里程碑意义的共同防御联盟后，中国于 7 月向南太平洋发射弹道导弹，引发了国际社会的广泛谴责。 在时任总理斯科特·莫里森 (Scott Morrison) 的领导下，新冠肺炎 (COVID-19) 疫情期间外交紧张局势达到顶峰后，阿尔巴尼亚政府寻求稳定与中国的关系。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 中国对澳大利亚出口产品实施了价值 200 亿美元的贸易制裁，但这些措施已慢慢取消。 中国是澳大利亚最大的贸易伙伴，也是该国约三分之一出口的目的地。 弗莱彻表示，中国并未放弃将澳大利亚拉近其轨道的希望，而澳大利亚则更专注于巩固当前的关系。 “但这种关系不太可能变得真正亲密——就像澳大利亚与其地区及其他地方志同道合的伙伴所享有的轻松、亲密的友谊一样，”他说。 “世界观和国家安全议程的分歧实在太大了。 “堪培拉追求这样的目标是毫无意义的；它认识到这一点并且是现实的。” 世界观的“不匹配”使得两国关系容易受到破坏，其主要风险包括新一轮严重分歧或爆发冲突，包括对台湾使用武力。 这位前外交官表示：“动乱或冲突总是有可能发生，尽管我认为目前可能性不大。” 弗莱彻表示，如果政策得到跨党派支持，并且政客们不“寻求利用困难谋取国内利益”，那么澳大利亚在面对中国时将会更加坚定。 “两党合作带来了政策的一致性，并限制了中国在澳大利亚体系内玩弄游戏的能力，”他说。 弗莱彻于 2019 年至 2023 年担任澳大利亚驻中国大使，并于 2014 年领导谈判团队，帮助两国签署了自由贸易协定……

reflection.en: When nations face a "gulf" in worldviews, the path to peace can seem daunting. Yahweh's word encourages us to pursue peace actively, recognizing that while complete agreement may not always be possible, our commitment to peaceful coexistence remains vital. This calls for wisdom and perseverance in navigating complex international relations.
reflection.zh: 当国家之间面临“世界观鸿沟”时，通往和平的道路可能显得令人生畏。雅伟的话语鼓励我们积极寻求和平，认识到虽然完全一致可能并非总是可行，但我们对和平共处的承诺至关重要。这要求我们在复杂的国际关系中运用智慧和毅力。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.

title.en: More than one million evacuated, flights cancelled, as Typhoon Dolphin hits China
title.zh: 台风“海豚”袭击中国，逾百万人撤离，航班取消

summary.en: Typhoon Dolphin has led to the evacuation of over one million people and the cancellation of flights in China. The cyclone previously swept across Japan, causing injuries to six people and cutting power to more than 50,000 buildings.
summary.zh: 台风“海豚”袭击中国，导致逾百万人撤离，航班取消。此前，该气旋已横扫日本，造成六人受伤，并导致超过五万栋建筑断电。

body.en:
Typhoon Dolphin brought heavy rain to eastern China on Monday, causing hundreds of flight cancellations even as the storm weakened and some cities resumed public transport.

The typhoon had already swept across Japan’s southern Okinawa prefecture, injuring six people and cutting power to more than 50,000 buildings.

It then made landfall near Yuhuan in eastern Zhejiang province on Sunday evening, China's meteorological authorities said.

The storm packed maximum sustained winds of 151km/h near its centre at landfall, equivalent to a Category 1 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson scale.

Authorities had moved offshore workers to safety, ordered vessels back to port and increased checks at reservoirs, mountain streams, landslide-prone areas, construction sites and tourist locations.

The weather system lost power after making landfall, with China's National Meteorological Centre (NMC) issuing its least severe typhoon alert on Monday morning.

However, the NMC warned that parts of east and central China would continue to receive heavy rain for the next day.

The typhoon had triggered a top-level alert over the weekend, prompting over 1,000 flight cancellations and tens of thousands of evacuations.

Transport was widely disrupted across the east of the country, and more than one million people were evacuated from their homes.

Nine hundred and forty-three flights from Shanghai's two main passenger airports were cancelled, the airport authority said in an online post.

A 42-year-old tourist from Guangdong said he was stranded in Shanghai after his family's flight, scheduled to depart on Sunday, was cancelled due to Typhoon Dolphin.

He said the family had been rebooked on a flight at 10pm on Monday, although they were unsure whether it would be able to take off.

"To us Guangdong people, this typhoon is as ordinary as having a meal and feeling the wind. It's just part of everyday life," he said, adding that the storm did not appear particularly strong by the standards of China's southern coast.

In neighbouring Zhejiang province, the city of Wenzhou relocated more than 900,000 residents and opened more than 1,000 emergency shelters.

In Fujian province, authorities evacuated 98,900 people from high-risk areas after raising the typhoon emergency response to Level 3, according to Xinhua. Zhejiang, Shanghai and Jiangsu have also activated Level 3 emergency responses.

Fujian maritime authorities said 55 coastal passenger ferry routes had been suspended, all 115 offshore construction projects had been halted, and 290 construction vessels had been moved to sheltered waters.

title.zh: 中国疏散一百万人，大规模风暴来袭

summary.en: Typhoon Dolphin has made landfall, bringing strong winds and heavy rain across eastern China, including Shanghai, leading to the evacuation of one million residents.
summary.zh: 台风“海豚”已登陆，给包括上海在内的中国东部地区带来了强风和暴雨，导致一百万居民被疏散。

body.en:
Chinese authorities have evacuated more than a million people from their homes in eastern China including the financial capital Shanghai, as Typhoon Dolphin made landfall.

The typhoon brought heavy rain and halted transportation across the region. Nearly 1,000 flights were cancelled in Shanghai alone on Monday.

While authorities have downgraded Dolphin to a tropical storm, they continue to warn of torrential rains, severe flooding and the risk of landslides through to Wednesday as the storm moves north.

Chinese authorities had earlier issued their highest-level red alert for Dolphin, which is the strongest storm to hit China this year.

It packed maximum wind speeds of 150km/h (94mph) when it first slammed into Yuhuan in the Zhejiang province at 17:30 (09:30 GMT) on Sunday before making a second landfall in the city of Wenzhou about an hour later, meteorological authorities said.

Heavy rain was forecast on Monday for the provinces of Shandong, Henan, Hubei, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang and the city of Shanghai.

Governments have urged people to avoid outdoor activities, while several top tourist attractions remain closed, including parts of Disneyland and Legoland, and several viewing platforms along the Bund in Shanghai.

Footage on state media show ground-floor businesses flooded in the former French Concession in Shanghai, an area popular with tourists, and people wading through ankle-deep waters.

Several state media outlets have reported that a nine-year-old boy from Wenling, Zhejiang is missing after being swept into the sea. Chinese officials have not reported any casualties.

Parts of Zhejiang could receive 250mm to 500mm of rain over the next few days, forecasters say.

Authorities in Hangzhou, Zhejiang's capital city, have waived parking fees in all public spaces for drivers seeking shelter amid the strong winds and floodwaters.

Elsewhere in the province, Wenzhou authorities have relocated some 900,000 residents and opened more than 1,000 emergency shelters, while about 390,000 people have been evacuated from their homes in the city of Taizhou.

In the coastal province of Fujian, maritime authorities have suspended dozens of passenger ferry routes and halted more than 100 offshore construction projects.

The storm moved over a long distance of 6,000km before making landfall, suggesting a lifespan of more than three times that of an average typhoon, according to China's state broadcaster CCTV.

It also has a massive circulation size and intense rainfall capacity, CCTV reported.

Misinformation around the storm has apparently spread rapidly on the Chinese internet, with state media reporting that two people have been detained for distributing such content.

body.zh: 随着台风海豚登陆，中国当局已从包括金融首都上海在内的中国东部地区疏散了超过一百万人。 台风带来大雨，导致该地区交通中断。周一仅上海就有近1000个航班被取消。 尽管当局已将“海豚”降级为热带风暴，但随着风暴向北移动，直到周三，他们仍继续警告暴雨、严重洪水和山体滑坡的风险。 中国当局早些时候发布了“海豚”的最高级别红色警报，这是今年袭击中国的最强风暴。 气象部门表示，周日 17:30（格林威治标准时间 09:30）首次登陆浙江省玉环市时，最大风速达到 150 公里/小时（94 英里/小时），大约一小时后第二次登陆温州市。 周一，山东、河南、湖北、安徽、江苏、浙江和上海市预计有大雨。 各国政府敦促人们避免户外活动，而几个顶级旅游景点仍然关闭，包括迪士尼乐园和乐高乐园的部分区域，以及上海外滩沿线的几个观景平台。 官方媒体的视频显示，上海前法租界的底层商铺被洪水淹没，该地区深受游客欢迎，人们涉过齐脚踝深的水域。 多家官方媒体报道称，浙江温岭一名九岁男孩被卷入海中失踪。中国官员尚未报告任何人员伤亡。 预报员称，未来几天浙江部分地区可能出现250毫米至500毫米的降雨。 浙江省会杭州市当局已免除所有公共场所的停车费，供在强风和洪水中寻求庇护的司机使用。 在省内其他地方，温州当局已重新安置约90万居民，并开设了1000多个紧急避难所，而台州市约39万人已从家中疏散。 在沿海省份福建，海事部门暂停了数十条客运轮渡航线，并叫停了100多个海上建设项目。 据中国国家电视台中央电视台报道，这场风暴在登陆前移动了6000公里的长距离，表明其寿命是普通台风的三倍多。 据中央电视台报道，它还具有巨大的环流规模和强大的降雨能力。 有关风暴的错误信息显然在中国互联网上迅速传播，官方媒体报道称，有两人因传播此类内容而被拘留。 其中一名 60 岁男子用人工智能制作了一段虚假视频，声称有人在……

reflection.en: As a massive typhoon forces millions from their homes, the fragility of human life in the face of nature's power becomes clear. In such moments of crisis and displacement, Psalm 46:1 reminds us that Yahweh is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in trouble. This promise offers a steadfast anchor for those facing uncertainty and seeking safety.
reflection.zh: 当一场巨大的台风迫使数百万人撤离家园时，人类在自然力量面前的脆弱性显而易见。在这样的危机和流离失所的时刻，诗篇46:1提醒我们，雅伟是我们的避难所和力量，是我们在患难中随时的帮助。这个应许为那些面临不确定性并寻求安全的人提供了一个坚定的锚。

verse.textEn: God is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in trouble.
verse.textZh: 神是我们的避难所，是我们的力量，是我们在患难中随时的帮助。

title.en: China: Typhoon Dolphin prompts mass evacuation, canceled flights
title.zh: 中国：台风海豚引发大规模疏散，航班取消

summary.en: Typhoon Dolphin is causing significant disruption across China, leading to the cancellation of nearly 1,500 flights in Shanghai and flood alerts in parts of Beijing, even as the storm begins to weaken.
summary.zh: 台风海豚正在中国各地造成严重破坏，尽管风力减弱，上海仍有近1500个航班被取消，北京部分地区也发布了洪水警报。

body.en:
Even as it weakens, Typhoon Dolphin is disrupting life in China. Close to 1,500 flights have been canceled in Shanghai while parts of Beijing are under flood alert.

Heavy rainfall and strong winds prompted flood alerts and more than 1,000 flight cancellations across China on Monday, even as Typhoon Dolphin weakened.

China's National Meteorological Centre (NMC) issued its least severe typhoon alert on Monday morning as the storm lost power after making landfall in China's Zhejiang Province on Sunday.

Despite the weaker storm, the NMC warned that parts of east and central China will continue to receive heavy rainfall. Authorities issued their most severe flash flood alert for parts of eastern and southern Zhejiang on Monday, state news broadcaster CCTV reported. 

Five districts in Beijing are also under red alerts for heavy rainfall on Monday, with risks of landslides and flooding.

The storm had already forced over 300,000 people in eastern China to preemptively relocate, while bringing heavy rainfall to northern Taiwan over the weekend. In Shanghai, authorities evacuated more than 30,000 people out of high-risk areas. Overall, some one million people have been told to seek shelter. 

Shanghai's two main passenger airports, Pudong International Airport and Hongqiao International Airport, canceled 943 flights between them for Monday, the airport authority said in a post online. That's a reduction of capacity by nearly 40%.

On Sunday, the two airports had cancelled nearly 1,500 flights, or about 60% of their scheduled travel, according to state media.

Public transport services in the city were also impacted, with several local trains suspended.

Zhejiang's Ningbo International Airport will resume flights midday on Monday but warned that some of the scheduled travel may still be delayed or canceled as the storm had "not yet completely dissipated."

China is dealing with Typhoon Dolphin just two weeks after Typhoon Noul struck its southern Guangdong province. Last month, Typhoon Maysak killed 11 people and injured over 300 in the central Hubei province.

Extreme weather systems are a common feature in China this time of the year, with typhoons leaving significant displacement , infrastructural damage and loss of lives. Scientists warn that the intensity and frequency of such extreme weather have increased and will continue to rise amid climate change.

title.en: Worldview 'gulf' behind strained Australia-China ties, former Australian ambassador says
title.zh: 前澳大利亚大使称，世界观“鸿沟”是澳中关系紧张的幕后原因

summary.en: Australia's former ambassador to China identified "diverging worldviews" as a key obstacle to fostering a robust relationship between the two nations.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚前驻华大使指出，“世界观差异”是澳中两国建立健康关系的主要障碍之一。

body.en:
Australia is unlikely ever to have a true partnership with China due to a mismatch of worldviews, rendering it pointless to pursue that goal, the nation's former top diplomat to China says.

But in an analysis piece for the Lowy Institute, Australia's former ambassador to China Graham Fletcher noted several wildcards, such as Chinese military action in Taiwan , could still disrupt the "modest new normal" of the relationship.

The change in government at the 2022 federal election acted as a circuit-breaker in increasingly fraught dealings between the nations, although they had still been marred by intimidatory military encounters involving Chinese forces, he said.

China sparked widespread international condemnation over its launch of a ballistic missile into the South Pacific in July following the signing of a landmark mutual defence alliance between Australia and Fiji.

The Albanese government sought to stabilise relations with China after diplomatic tensions peaked during the COVID-19 pandemic under then-prime minister Scott Morrison's leadership.

China slapped $20 billion in trade sanctions on Australian exports, measures that have slowly been wound back.

China is Australia's largest trading partner and is the destination for about a third of the nation's exports.

Fletcher said China had not given up hope of drawing Australia closer into its orbit, while Australia was more focused on consolidating its current relationship.

"But this relationship is unlikely ever to become genuinely close — like the relaxed, intimate fellowship Australia enjoys with like-minded partners elsewhere in its region and beyond," he said.

"The gulf in terms of diverging world views and national security agendas is simply too wide.

"It would be pointless for Canberra to pursue such a goal; it recognises this and is realistic."

The "mismatch" of world views made the relationship vulnerable to disruption, with key risks including another round of serious disagreements or the cataclysm of a conflict, including the use of force against Taiwan.

"An upheaval or conflict is always a possibility, though not in my opinion a strong one at present," the former diplomat said.

Australia would be on firmer ground when facing China if policies had cross-party support and politicians did not "seek to exploit difficulties for domestic advantage", Fletcher said.

"Bipartisanship produces policy consistency and limits China's ability to play games within the Australian system," he said.

body.zh: 澳大利亚前驻华最高外交官表示，由于世界观不匹配，澳大利亚不太可能与中国建立真正的伙伴关系，因此追求这一目标毫无意义。 但澳大利亚前驻华大使格雷厄姆·弗莱彻在洛伊研究所的一篇分析文章中指出，一些不确定因素，例如中国在台湾的军事行动，仍然可能破坏两国关系的“适度新常态”。 他说，2022 年联邦选举中的政府更迭为两国之间日益令人担忧的交易起到了断路器的作用，尽管它们仍然受到涉及中国军队的恐吓性军事冲突的损害。 在澳大利亚和斐济签署具有里程碑意义的共同防御联盟后，中国于 7 月向南太平洋发射弹道导弹，引发了国际社会的广泛谴责。 在时任总理斯科特·莫里森 (Scott Morrison) 的领导下，新冠肺炎 (COVID-19) 疫情期间外交紧张局势达到顶峰后，阿尔巴尼亚政府寻求稳定与中国的关系。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 中国对澳大利亚出口产品实施了价值 200 亿美元的贸易制裁，但这些措施已慢慢取消。 中国是澳大利亚最大的贸易伙伴，也是该国约三分之一出口的目的地。 弗莱彻表示，中国并未放弃将澳大利亚拉近其轨道的希望，而澳大利亚则更专注于巩固当前的关系。 “但这种关系不太可能变得真正亲密——就像澳大利亚与其地区及其他地方志同道合的伙伴所享有的轻松、亲密的友谊一样，”他说。 “世界观和国家安全议程的分歧实在太大了。 “堪培拉追求这样的目标是毫无意义的；它认识到这一点并且是现实的。” 世界观的“不匹配”使得两国关系容易受到破坏，其主要风险包括新一轮严重分歧或爆发冲突，包括对台湾使用武力。 这位前外交官表示：“动乱或冲突总是有可能发生，尽管我认为目前可能性不大。” 弗莱彻表示，如果政策得到跨党派支持，并且政客们不“寻求利用困难谋取国内利益”，那么澳大利亚在面对中国时将会更加坚定。 “两党合作带来了政策的一致性，并限制了中国在澳大利亚体系内玩弄游戏的能力，”他说。 弗莱彻于 2019 年至 2023 年担任澳大利亚驻中国大使，并于 2014 年领导谈判团队，帮助两国签署了自由贸易协定……

reflection.en: When nations face a "gulf" in worldviews, the path to peace can seem daunting. Yahweh's word encourages us to pursue peace actively, recognizing that while complete agreement may not always be possible, our commitment to peaceful coexistence remains vital. This calls for wisdom and perseverance in navigating complex international relations.
reflection.zh: 当国家之间面临“世界观鸿沟”时，通往和平的道路可能显得令人生畏。雅伟的话语鼓励我们积极寻求和平，认识到虽然完全一致可能并非总是可行，但我们对和平共处的承诺至关重要。这要求我们在复杂的国际关系中运用智慧和毅力。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.en: More than one million evacuated, flights cancelled, as Typhoon Dolphin hits China
title.zh: 台风“海豚”袭击中国，逾百万人撤离，航班取消

summary.en: Typhoon Dolphin has led to the evacuation of over one million people and the cancellation of flights in China. The cyclone previously swept across Japan, causing injuries to six people and cutting power to more than 50,000 buildings.
summary.zh: 台风“海豚”袭击中国，导致逾百万人撤离，航班取消。此前，该气旋已横扫日本，造成六人受伤，并导致超过五万栋建筑断电。

body.en:
Typhoon Dolphin brought heavy rain to eastern China on Monday, causing hundreds of flight cancellations even as the storm weakened and some cities resumed public transport.

The typhoon had already swept across Japan’s southern Okinawa prefecture, injuring six people and cutting power to more than 50,000 buildings.

It then made landfall near Yuhuan in eastern Zhejiang province on Sunday evening, China's meteorological authorities said.

The storm packed maximum sustained winds of 151km/h near its centre at landfall, equivalent to a Category 1 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson scale.

Authorities had moved offshore workers to safety, ordered vessels back to port and increased checks at reservoirs, mountain streams, landslide-prone areas, construction sites and tourist locations.

The weather system lost power after making landfall, with China's National Meteorological Centre (NMC) issuing its least severe typhoon alert on Monday morning.

However, the NMC warned that parts of east and central China would continue to receive heavy rain for the next day.

The typhoon had triggered a top-level alert over the weekend, prompting over 1,000 flight cancellations and tens of thousands of evacuations.

Transport was widely disrupted across the east of the country, and more than one million people were evacuated from their homes.

Nine hundred and forty-three flights from Shanghai's two main passenger airports were cancelled, the airport authority said in an online post.

A 42-year-old tourist from Guangdong said he was stranded in Shanghai after his family's flight, scheduled to depart on Sunday, was cancelled due to Typhoon Dolphin.

He said the family had been rebooked on a flight at 10pm on Monday, although they were unsure whether it would be able to take off.

title.en: From petitions to memes: How students made dissent visible
title.zh: 从请愿到网络迷因：学生如何让异议显现

summary.en: Student movements throughout history, from imperial China to modern India, have consistently found new ways to express dissent and challenge established authority, adapting their methods to contemporary tools and symbols.
summary.zh: 从中国古代到当今印度，学生运动不断调整其工具和象征，以挑战权威，使异议得以显现。

body.en:
From imperial China to present-day India, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols of their age to challenge authority.

On July 22, 2026, in rainy Mumbai, India , a casually dressed young woman stepped in front of a slow-moving police van carrying detained students. She placed her palm on the hood, forcing the vehicle to stop.

Mobile phones captured the moment from every angle. She too, raised her own phone and recorded the encounter. Within hours, the clip spread across India and beyond.

It became one of the defining visuals of the Cockroach Janta Party protests, a movement in which students demanded transparency and accountability, following leaks in India's medical entrance exams.

But the power of the moment lay not only in what she did, but in how quickly it was seen. A single gesture, a young woman confronting authority , became a symbol shared across millions of screens.

While the clip belongs to a generation raised on social media, the impulse behind it is much older.

From court petitions and revolutionary posters to photographs, umbrellas and memes, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols available to them, turning them into vehicles for dissent.

Long before television or social media carried dissent across borders, students still found ways to make their grievances heard.

In Eastern Han China, for instance, scholars at the Imperial Academy (Taixue) aligned with reform-minded officials in opposing powerful eunuchs at court, whom many viewed as corrupt and politically overbearing.

They voiced their objections through public criticism, political networks and petitions.

In an era when political communication moved through official channels, petitions were among the established ways of bringing grievances before the throne. Written in formal language and delivered through the bureaucracy, they carried student concerns directly into the state's communication system.

In Paris in 1968, students challenged university authorities and a conservative postwar social order. As demonstrations spread across the French capital and drew in workers, one of the movement's most enduring contributions emerged from a basement workshop at the Ecole des Beaux-Arts.

The Atelier Populaire ("People's Workshop") printed thousands of posters during the protests, many of them overnight. Their bold graphics, silhouettes and slogans became the visual language of the movement. Produced collectively, many carried no individual author's name, helping transform protest into a shared public voice.

The posters and their messages could appear in dozens of places overnight, giving the protest a wide local visual presence.

Protests also became more impactful when images could be transmitted across borders.

title.en: Albanese, Japan's PM and melons: Behind the revived row over podcast remark

body.en:
Opposition leader Angus Taylor has called on Anthony Albanese to personally apologise for remarks the prime minister made about two crown melons gifted to him by his Japanese counterpart.

The criticism follows an opinion piece by former Japanese ambassador to Australia Shingo Yamagami, published in The Australian on Monday, which criticised comments Albanese made during a podcast interview last month with comedian Nikki Osborne.

Albanese was discussing two crown melons gifted to him by Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi during her visit to Australia in May, gesturing near his chest as he spoke about the fruit, which he said was a "pretty strange" gift but ended up being "quite good".

Yamagami said the remarks failed to recognise the gift's cultural significance and risked undermining Australia’s close relationship with Japan.

He said crown melons are highly prized in Japan, and the fruit gifted to Albanese was carefully cultivated in a specialised greenhouse.

Yamagami also highlighted Takaichi's position as Japan's first female prime minister, noting she had previously faced derogatory comments about her gender, including from Chinese officials.

"The last thing she expected was to be so casually mocked by the trusted leader of Japan’s special strategic partner," Yamagami wrote.

During Albanese's appearance on the podcast, Osborne asked the prime minister what the "most crap gift you've ever received on an overseas jaunt" was.

Albanese said he'd received a gift recently that was "pretty strange that ended up being quite good", explaining that he'd been given was a melon from Takaichi during her visit to Australia in May.

Osborne responded by asking him how the Japanese leader got the fruit into Australia.

"Did she smuggle it?" the podcast host asked, gesturing toward her abdomen, joking that Takaichi could have said she was pregnant.

"I don't know, 'I got a couple of melons,'" Albanese replied, while smiling and making hand gestures that some critics have interpreted as an inappropriate reference to breasts.

Osborne then replied: "She brought two? She just came in looking like Pamela Anderson."

Responding to suggestions that the prime minister's hand gestures were referencing Takaichi's chest, a spokesperson for Albanese told SBS News "the assertion is incorrect".

Last month, a widely shared Facebook post had falsely claimed that Albanese compared Takaichi's breasts to Anderson's.

body.en:
South Australia is launching a royal commission into artificial intelligence , with the state government seeking to shape how the rapidly developing technology is used and regulated.

Premier Peter Malinauskas says AI presents major opportunities, but warns unchecked development could pose risks to society and the future of work.

"We can choose to allow this industry to come to our country and evolve in a way that is unregulated and unchecked," he said.

"Or we can choose to set the agenda … to ensure that we use AI in a way that puts people first."

The inquiry is expected to begin in October and deliver its final report by 1 July 2027. It's expected to focus on the economic and social opportunities the technology provides for the state.

With artificial intelligence already changing workplaces, education, healthcare and government, experts told SBS News that the royal commission will be forced to address a sweeping range of issues.

But why is South Australia launching its own state-based royal commission, what will it investigate, and what can it realistically achieve?

Malinauskas says Australia is at a "fork in the road" over how AI should be developed and governed.

The premier told the media on Monday that he wants South Australia to establish safeguards around the technology while positioning the state to benefit from its economic opportunities.

The announcement follows his recent trip to the United States, where he met with major technology companies including OpenAI, Anthropic and Apple.

During the trip, Malinauskas visited OpenAI's headquarters in San Francisco and signed a memorandum of understanding with the company's co-founder and president Greg Brockman.

Anton van den Hengel, chief scientist at the Australian Institute for Machine Learning, told SBS News that South Australia was well-placed to benefit from the technology because of its existing AI research and startup ecosystem.

The South Australian government has backed AI since 2018, he said, while the state had strong research, technical and research translation capabilities, as well as a "brilliant set of start-ups".

"For a long time, Australia's geography has been limitation rather than opportunity. One of the many benefits of AI is that that's no longer the case. We're very well placed to participate in the upside of AI."

He said the royal commission would offer a chance "to make sure that we all benefit from the opportunities".

title.en: The alternative to upping interest rates that would leave us with more cash
title.zh: 加息的替代方案：让我们拥有更多现金

summary.en: Raising compulsory super could do the same job as raising interest rates — but the money is yours. So why aren't we talking about it?
summary.zh: 提高强制性养老金可以起到与提高利率相同的效果——但钱是你的。那么，我们为什么不讨论它呢？

body.en:
Share your feedback and help us improve this feature. Read more about how we use AI at SBS here.

Every time the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) meets to discuss the cash rate, millions of Australians hold their breath, knowing the outcome could affect their mortgage repayments , savings and household budgets.

Some economists say there's another way to cool spending — one that builds your retirement savings instead of handing more money to the bank through higher interest rates.

The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) is due to hand down its next cash rate decision on Tuesday. Financial markets and most economists expect the RBA to leave the cash rate unchanged as inflation continues to ease, although the board has indicated it remains focused on returning inflation to its 2 to 3 per cent target.

Cooling inflation means squeezing demand somewhere. While governments can also influence demand through fiscal policy, such as changing taxes or government spending, it's now largely the RBA's job to adjust the cash rate to make borrowing more expensive. Higher interest rates can also strengthen the Australian dollar , making imports cheaper and reducing the demand for exports.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

But this design hits homeowners in Australia harder than it does in many other countries, economist Chris Richardson says.

"Because we haven't built enough homes, Australia has really high housing prices and a lot of debt around that. And our interest rates are tied to short-term interest rates. So when we fight inflation, it tends to fall more on the shoulders of mortgage holders than you see in most other nations," he tells SBS News.

Richardson believes there's another lever that could be used instead of or alongside the cash rate: superannuation. Lift compulsory super contributions temporarily, and households would have less money to spend, helping cool demand, he says.

The difference is where the money goes — not interest to a bank, but savings for your own retirement.

Supporters say it could spread the burden of fighting inflation beyond borrowers. Critics argue it would simply shift the costs elsewhere. Here's how the idea stacks up.

The super guarantee (SG) is the compulsory minimum share of wages employers pay into eligible workers' superannuation. summary.en: The Census raises some questions and a few myths. Here's what you need to know.

body.en:
In 2021, more than 25 million Australians shared information about their personal lives, families, and occupations as part of the Census of Population and Housing .

Data collected by the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) painted a detailed picture of the nation's diversity.

Almost half of all Australians had a parent born overseas, and more than 400 languages were spoken , including over 180 Indigenous languages.

On Tuesday 11 August, people will again be asked to share information about their lives for the 2026 Census.

The questionnaire is compulsory for everyone in Australia on Census night, including international visitors, refugees and migrants.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Here are some of the most common Census myths and questions — and what an expert says about them.

Emily Walter, a Census national spokesperson at the ABS, said there are misconceptions that the Census is a test or graded assessment tool.

"This is a self-reported questionnaire ... so, the right answer is always what represents you the best and who you are," she told SBS Examines.

The more honestly people answered, the more accurately the data reflected Australia's population, she added.

"It's really important that we understand how our cultural makeup is changing and everyone's individual responses contribute to that ... [and] provides the opportunity for local services to be provided."

Information collected during the Census cannot be shared with police, immigration agents or any other government departments.

By law, personal information, including names and addresses, must be separated from other Census data.

After the Census, names can be retained for up to 18 months, and addresses for up to 36 months.

The ABS has spent years assessing the privacy, security and processing of its data, with all information collected during the Census protected under the Census and Statistics Act.

The Census is often referred to as a national headcount or a snapshot of the nation, but it's used to inform funding for essential services like schools, hospitals, libraries and public transportation.

Walter said people's responses influenced the location and availability of English classes for newly settled migrants, which "help them then build their language skills and support them through applying for jobs or driver's licences or all of the things that you need to support yourself".

She added that Census responses cannot be used to make a person attend English language classes.

The Census must be completed in English; however, information about the survey is available on the Census website in 26 languages.

body.en:

What do extreme sports, doomscrolling, addiction, Parkinson's disease, and ADHD all have in common? Dopamine. This crucial neurotransmitter helps facilitate reward, motivation, memory and movement within the body, but are its effects always beneficial? Watch Insight episode Chasing Dopamine Tuesday 11 August 8.30pm on SBS or SBS On Demand.

When Glenn Peterson started on a higher dosage of medication to treat his Parkinson's disease symptoms, he didn't expect the consequences it would have.

"I'd see a horse race, and I'd want the thrill of it winning, and betting on it. I had constant thoughts of sex as well, which never entered my mind prior to that. I couldn't get rid of it."

The 73-year-old was diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease eight years ago. He was taking a dopamine precursor medication — a drug the body converts to dopamine when it reaches the brain — to treat his symptoms. He was later prescribed a dopamine agonist as well to make treatment more effective.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

While the brain converts dopamine precursors directly into dopamine, dopamine-agonist medications mimic dopamine by activating dopamine receptors in the brain.

When combined, these drugs help treat the motor symptoms of Parkinson's, a progressive brain disorder that damages dopamine-producing neurons, but research shows agonist drugs can cause the development of compulsive and addictive behaviours.

Glenn says when the dopamine-agonist medication was increased, he developed these behaviours.

Glenn's wife, Robyn, also noticed the change when he started getting up in the middle of the night for hours at a time.

"And it started to come out that he was playing games ... or he'd gamble on the poker machines on his iPad through the night or go onto porn sites."

Glenn couldn’t understand why his mind seemed to turn against him. But when he revealed the extent of his newly developed compulsive behaviours to Robyn, she remembered the doctors had warned them that taking dopamine-agonist medication could bring on these side-effects.

They spoke to Glenn's neurologist and decreased his dose, which put an end to the compulsive behaviours.

Dopamine is a neurotransmitter in the brain that is involved in several of the body's functions, including movement — and contributes to our motivation and reward systems.
